identified_issues: State-observation conflation by the operations monitor, treating a synchronous transport-layer HTTP 504 gateway timeout as proof of underlying settlement failure.
Improper rollback proposal that would desynchronize the core ledger from the clearing network, causing duplicate payments or financial imbalance.
Failure of the automated monitoring alert to incorporate the authoritative out-of-band reconciliation surface (CAMT.053 / MT940 bilateral statement) before asserting non-settlement.
evidence: Clearing Bank SFTP Bilateral Statement (CAMT.053 / MT940 End-of-Window Feed at 08:30:00Z) explicitly confirms REF=TX-8102-EUR with CLEARING_ID=EBA-STEP2-9948102, AMT=14850000.00 EUR, STATUS=SETTLED, and VAL_DATETIME=2026-10-06T08:15:02Z.
Bilateral statement reports REJECTION_RECORDS: NONE, confirming the instruction was neither rejected nor cancelled.
Core Financial Ledger Engine record TX-8102-EUR reflects COMMITTED state with journal timestamp 2026-10-06T08:15:00.120Z, consistent with clearing value timestamp 08:15:02Z.
Outbound Payment Gateway HTTP 504 timeout occurred at 2026-10-06T08:15:03.205Z, five seconds after submission, representing a transport receipt disconnect rather than network clearing rejection.
recommended_action: Reject the proposed ledger rollback and clear the operations alert. Update the operations monitor to prevent proxy-state conflation by enforcing reconciliation against authoritative end-of-window CAMT.053/MT940 statements prior to evaluating batch settlement failure.
